subject: Hierarchical  binomial with group-level predictors: Optimizing and predicting for new groups

messages.author: d91df306d26cf161
messages.subject: Hierarchical  binomial with group-level predictors: Optimizing and predicting for new groups
parts:
Hello,

I am attempting to fit a hierarchical multilevel binomial model with group-level predictors*, then use the resulting model to simulate predicted values for new groups.

 

My first issue is that the sampling is terribly slow, averaging about 8 samples/chain/minute while running 3 chains in parallel on 3 cores (2015 MacBook pro, 16gb ram, 2.9 GHz Intel Core i5). My dataset is fairly large (6300 rows) and I have 3 individual-level predictors and 2 group-level predictors with all interactions included within each level. I think I've implemented Matt's trick correctly, but is there some other way to speed up the sampling? I am also getting rather low n_eff, usually around 3000-5000 for 22,500 total post-warmup draws. 

 

My second issue is that ultimately I would like to simulate predicted values for new groups with new data matrices of group- and individual level-predictors. I couldn't find any examples online of this type of predictions so I would love some validation that I wrote that section correctly in the "generated quantities" block.

 

Thank you very much,

Sam

 

*Background: The data come from a series of replicated experiments on the survival of crab larvae exposed to ultraviolet radiation. Experiments were conducted on different days (hence varying intercept for experiment) and on a total of 11 species of crabs. Larvae were grouped 4/chamber and the survival in individual chambers (replicates) was tracked over 3 days. Group (species)-level predictors are degree of pigmentation (proportion cover) and size of larvae of each species. Individual-level predictors are days of exposure, UV treatment (coded as 0, 1, or 2 for no UV, UVA, or UVA+UVB respectively), and cumulative light exposure (quantitative index of sun exposure).

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Hierarchical  binomial with group-level predictors: Optimizing and predicting for new groups
parts:
It's hard to follow long programs, though much easier than trying
to tease apart fragments.

You can run into slow sampling if you run out of memory and have
to start swapping. You might test relative speed of running one
chain at a time (3 is probably too many for an i5 as I think they
only have 2 cores---again, it's an empirical question that depends on
your CPU and memory speed).

How fast is it without the generated quantities? You want to pull
repeated arithmetic out of loops:

for (j in 1:S_N_Species)
S_bet[j,] = multi_normal_cholesky_rng((S_U[j,] * gam)', diag_pre_multiply(tau, omegaL))';

So do that multiplication of tau and omegaL outside of the loop.
And try to avoid all the transpositions by rearraning the ata where possible.
And you can probably just do S_U * gam and store it in a local variable
rather than trying to slice it apart by row (inefficient because Eigen stores
matrices column-major).

And there are more efficient ways to generate multinormals than
multi_normal_cholesky---I think the GP sections of the manual explain
some alternatives, but I can't recall --- the idea is to generate
a standard normal and then transform (rotate and scale) by covariance.

There are other things you could do to reduce some
redundant calcs, such as storing

bet[Species[n]]' + B

for all the species then indexing in the 1:N loop, but unless N is much
greater than the number of species, that won't help much.

- Bob

add includes --- please switch to using // for line comments.

Hi Bob,

Thank you very much for your help. I made the changes you suggested and sped up the model by 2-3x. I have another problem: one of the varying intercepts in my model (Experiment) is coming out highly correlated with my global fixed intercept (B[1]). Is there any way to control for this, or prohibit it from happening? I wrote the model with a global fixed intercept to force the varying intercepts to be offsets from this global intercept and centered at 0.

Thank you,
Sam
